title: Master the Linux Network Troubleshooting Ladder

scenes.line1: Why do pros use a troubleshooting ladder?
scenes.say: Ever get stuck debugging network issues? What’s the right order to check things in Linux?

rows.b: Is it up? Has an IP?

scenes.say: Work bottom-up: interface, gateway, DNS, remote port, local listener, firewall, and finally, packets. Each step narrows the problem.

scenes.title: Ladder in Action
scenes.say: Use real commands at each step. For example, check your interface with i-p a, ping the gateway, run dig for DNS, and netcat for remote ports.

scenes.question: What’s the first thing to check?
scenes.right: Always start at the interface: is it up and has an IP?
scenes.say: Interview trap: Don’t jump to DNS or firewall. Always start at the interface. That’s what interviewers want to hear.
